title: Operator VPC quickstart checklist (PRD draft)
content:
Context:
This is a pragmatic operator-facing quickstart checklist for onboarding a customer-managed VPC (private deployment) into Redwood Inference. Goal is to provide a concise, actionable sequence for SREs and solutions engineers to get a private deployment from 'network handed over' to 'healthy, auditable, and monitored' in a reproducible way. This doc is intentionally lightweight compared to fuller PRDs; it focuses on observable outcomes, minimum safe approvals, and audit signal requirements.

Audience:
- SRE / Oncall engineers running initial network handovers
- Solutions Engineers doing first-run installs for enterprise customers
- Security reviewers verifying audit coverage and approval artifacts

High-level objectives:
1) Validate customer-managed networking is configured to Redwood minimums (routing, DNS, firewall).
2) Ensure audit logging is enabled end-to-end (control plane events, connectivity checks, operator approvals) and exported to customer or Redwood log sink per contract.
3) Gate production-facing traffic behind a verifiable approval step (approval gates) with immutable artifacts.
4) Provide rollback steps and a post-onboarding verification plan (SLIs/SLOs, telemetry).

Minimum prerequisites (before operator begins):
- Customer has submitted completed VPC intake form (link in linked_artifacts).
- Customer has configured KMS/HSM and shared encryption keys or agreed Redwood-managed KMS per contract.
- Network topology diagram received and uploaded to the ticket.
- Emergency contact list and change window agreed.

Operator quickstart checklist (step-by-step):
1) Pre-checks (0-60m)
   - Confirm VPC CIDR, subnets, route tables, and NAT/IGW configuration match intake form. Note discrepancies in ticket.
   - Verify peering/transit connectivity if applicable. Run traceroutes and capture results.
   - Ensure customer ACLs allow control-plane IP ranges and NTP/DNS to Redwood endpoints.
   - Take initial snapshot: create a single JSON blob with preflight results (ipsec-trace.txt, route-table.json, dns-check.txt) and upload to ticket.

2) Approvals and gating (must be recorded in audit log)
   - Open approval in Approval System (see Jira JIRA-PRIV-2110 for template).
   - Required approvers: Solutions Engineering lead OR SRE on-call AND Security reviewer. Approval must include time window and expected downtime (if any).
   - Use ephemeral approval token feature (operator issues one-time bootstrap token). Record token id in ticket.
   - Log approval artifact to control-plane audit stream and attach the control-plane event id to the ticket.

3) Bootstrap connectivity (15-90m)
   - Create initial control-plane endpoint (private endpoint inside customer VPC) using bootstrap token.
   - Run health-checks: control-plane handshake, TLS cert validation, and KV cache warmup.
   - Verify mTLS between control-plane and agent nodes (if on-prem agents are used). Store mTLS cert fingerprints in ticket.

4) Audit and observability configuration (concurrent with bootstrap)
   - Enable control-plane audit logging: ensure control-plane events (deploy, approve, rollback, config-change) are emitted to both Redwood audit stream and customer log sink if requested.
   - Confirm network flow logs are enabled (VPC Flow Logs or equivalent).
   - Configure sampling for high-volume events: default 1% sampling for token-level traces, 100% for approval/rollback events.
   - Set up temporary debug-level traces for first 24 hours, with automatic backoff to info-level after 24h.

5) Functional validation (30-120m)
   - Run canonical acceptance prompts against the hosted model to validate end-to-end inference path. Record latency/throughput.
   - Verify cost-metering: token usage appears in billing events; reconcile with test traffic.
   - Run failure injection: simulate a control-plane failover and verify automatic fallback to allowed model variant.

6) Post-onboarding checks and handoff (within 24h)
   - Confirm CR (change record) and timestamped approval artifacts are attached to ticket.
   - Create a short-run monitoring playbook for customer: alert thresholds (latency p95 > X ms, token-errors > Y/min, CPU/GPU thermal alerts), retention for audit logs, and escalation path.
   - Schedule 48-hour follow-up call and 7-day review.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before marking onboarding complete):
- Approval artifact present and logged: approval id + timestamp + approver names.
- Audit logs for control-plane events captured and searchable for the retention specified by contract.
- End-to-end inference smoke test passes (happy-path prompts) with p50/p95 within SLO and no functional regressions.
- Billing events for test traffic appear and reconcile within 10% of measured tokens.
- Post-onboarding monitoring configured and alerts verified.

Rollback plan (fast path):
- If network misconfig prevents control-plane connectivity, revoke bootstrap token and revert any route changes. Use control-plane event id to mark rollback.
- If cert or KMS mismatch detected, rotate to previous known-good certs/keys and notify Security immediately.
- If resource contention or thermal failures occur, scale down traffic by returning to soft-rate limit and engage infra oncall.

Telemetry & SLOs to validate onboarding health:
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms for short prompts (configurable by customer).
- Error rate SLO: 0.2% 5xx per minute during onboarding test window.
- Audit log availability: events delivered to Redwood and customer sink within 60s 99% of the time over first 24h.

Risk matrix (quick):
- Missing audit coverage: High risk. Mitigation = require audit events as gating criteria before production traffic.
- Approval token leakage: High risk. Mitigation = ephemeral tokens + mandatory rotation + recording to audit stream.
- Customer network ACLs blocking telemetry: Medium risk. Mitigation = pre-flight checklist and traceroutes captured.

Operational notes / operator tips:
- Keep a persistent template for the "preflight snapshot"—operators should not freely edit the schema of the snapshot.
- Attach all relevant Slack thread links and PR IDs to the ticket so the audit trail is centralized.
- When in doubt, pause and escalate; it is cheaper to delay onboarding by an hour than to recover from an audit gap.

Open questions (to resolve in subsequent PRD):
- Should approval tokens be single-use or time-limited with auto-expire? Current prototype supports both; need product decision.
- Default sampling rate for trace-level token events during onboarding vs. steady-state.
- Who retains ultimate custody of audit logs when contract stipulates dual retention (customer + Redwood)?--clear policy needed.

Next steps / owner assignments:
- Maya Chen: iterate this checklist into the official runbook and convert into a Confluence playbook (due 2026-03-01).
- Ravi Patel: prototype auto-attachment of approval artifact ids to onboarding ticket (JIRA-PRIV-2110).
- Jordan Lee: add lightweight diagnostics CLI for preflight snapshot (issue created: JIRA-PRIV-2124).

Notes / references:
- See linked confluence page for longer onboarding PRD (design rationale, compliance artifacts).
- See infra PR for ephemeral approval tokens in linked_artifacts.

Draft status: lightweight draft intended for immediate use by SEs and SREs. Will be expanded after first three onboardings to include measured thresholds and refined rollback scripts.
